sn52.4:1.1: At one time the venerables Anuruddha, Sāriputta, and Mahāmoggallāna were staying near Sāketa, in the Thorny Wood.
sn52.4:1.2: Then in the late afternoon, Sāriputta and Mahāmoggallāna came out of retreat, went to Anuruddha, and exchanged greetings with him.
sn52.4:1.3: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. Sāriputta said to Anuruddha:
sn52.4:1.4: “Reverend Anuruddha, what things should a trainee meditator enter and remain in?”
sn52.4:2.1: “Reverend Sāriputta, a trainee meditator should enter and remain in the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.
sn52.4:2.3: It’s when a meditator meditates by observing an aspect of the body—ardently aware and understanding, without craving and aversion towards the world <span class=
sn52.4:2.4: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …
sn52.4:2.6: principles—ardently aware and understanding, without craving and aversion towards the world <span class=
sn52.4:2.7: A trainee meditator should enter and remain in these four kinds of mindfulness meditation.”
